articles.title: We asked real people what they’re wearing this fall – burgundy, secretly comfy pants and fierce boots
articles.summary: I chased down people on weekdays, interrupting their brisk walks and lunch breaks to ask them to share details of their fall outfits. ‘Is nonstick cookware safe?’ Send us your food safety questions.
body: I t’s October and New Yorkers have finally retired the breezy pants and linen button-downs required to brave stuffy subway stations. Like much of the US, we’re now tasked with expertly layering for autumn’s up-and-down weather while still looking put together for the workday.

You might also be staring down your closet’s sea of denim and bulky coats, wondering what to wear. Instead of consulting the runways or analyzing the latest fashion trends, I wandered through Manhattan’s financial district, which boasts millions of square feet in office space, to ask people about their outfits.

I chased down people on weekdays, interrupting their brisk walks and, most likely, their lunch breaks. Below, New Yorkers (and two visitors) share the details of their fall outfits. We couldn’t find exact matches for many of the items, so we linked to similar options, usually from the brands that they recommended.

articles.title: Modern life is stuck in a sea of sameness. The pursuit of beauty is a necessary antidote | Brigid Delaney
articles.summary: Everything has become so frictionless and optimised, that concerted efforts must be made to turn back towards beauty and individuality – even if it has no explicit market value. By the time it’s 5pm on a Friday, the headache and dry eyes have well and truly settled in.
body: To lift your spirits, you decide to treat yourself to a weekend at a beachside Airbnb.

But the town is not how you remember it as a kid. The farmland has been turned into identical housing estates broken up by highway-hugging shopping centres with the same Guzman, Woolies, Chemist Warehouse, Dan Murphy’s and Priceline as all the other shopping centres.
They’re not the only things that are samey. The cars in the car park are mostly white or grey, and stepping out of them, people are in near-identical athleisure or shorts and T-shirts.

The Airbnb is how it was depicted in the pictures (minimalist, fancy handwash in the bathroom, Anko soft furnishings) but there is something dispiriting about it. Just like the cars, the interior is grey and white, and it smells of surface cleaner. It’s a house devoid of colour, personality and character.
points: Everything has become so frictionless and optimised, that concerted efforts must be made to turn back towards beauty and individuality – even if it has no explicit market value.

articles.title: Experts cast doubt on Anthropic report detailing how AI has altered work at the company
articles.summary: Anthropic claims AI will shift how work gets done and labor demand – but some experts are skeptical of the vision. Last year, the Anthropic CEO, Dario Amodei, warned that artificial intelligence could eliminate half of entry-level white-collar jobs and that in six months it would be writing 90% of…
body: Now, in a report Anthropic published on Thursday, the company said it was hiring fewer junior technical workers and that human attention has become the new “bottleneck” as it increasingly relies on its Claude AI agents.

Anthropic says AI has changed the way work gets done, and as a result, restructured employment at the company. The report suggests its changes foreshadow the future of work more broadly: as more companies adopt AI agents, software engineers could face a tougher job market while entry-level tech workers struggle to build necessary skills and experience.

“As AI diffuses and improves, the organization of work could shift,” Anthropic’s report reads before offering a potential future. “One possibility is single-person startups, each with a human founder steering swarms of agents to rake in billions in revenue.”

In its report, Anthropic touts its “deep adoption of AI”, which it claims resulted in “producing more code per person, closing more sales per rep, and processing more contracts”. By outsourcing some coding and sales-related tasks to AI agents, Anthropic said it raised productivity within a few months.

articles.title: Crowded nest? How parents and their adult kids can live together in peace
articles.summary: With record numbers of adult children living at home with their parents, how can this arrangement work for everyone? Set ground rules from the off, respect each other’s privacy, and don’t revert to type, say the experts.
body: Whether they are fresh out of university and looking for a job, have recently been made redundant, are saving to buy a home or newly divorced, it’s becoming increasingly common for adult children to live at home with their parents. According to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), 35% of men and 22% of women aged between 20 and 34 were living with their parents in 2025.

I speak from experience: my younger sister lived at home with my mother for two years while she did her PhD, and I moved home for almost three years after becoming a single mother postpartum. In both of our situations, it would have been good to have some practical advice to make it work, with tensions sometimes running high and arguments inevitable.

If parents and their adult children are going to coexist successfully, honest communication is essential from the outset. How long do children expect to stay? Will they contribute financially? Will they do any housework? Are guests allowed? Difficulties will arise if you aren’t clear about these boundaries from the off.

articles.title: The Garmin Cirqa Finally Got a Much-Needed Feature
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. This week Garmin's screenless Cirqa smart band received a firmware update that fixes one of its most obvious gaps: the lack of alerts from your phone.
body: Amusingly, Garmin's own FAQ still states that the Cirqa does not vibrate for text messages, phone calls, or other smartphone notifications. Clearly that page is now out of date, so Garmin will want to correct it. Since Garmin doesn't yet have step-by-step instructions, I tested the text-message vibrations myself. Here's how you can set up your Cirqa smart band to vibrate for calls and texts, in addition to a number of other promising updates to check out.
To receive these alerts, your band must be running firmware 4.20 or later. Here is how to get everything configured.
Update the firmware. Open your Garmin Connect app and sync your Cirqa, so the app can check for and install version 4.20 or newer.
Grant the necessary phone permissions. In your phone's settings, make sure Garmin Connect has permission to access SMS, Contacts, and Phone.

articles.title: Byredo’s Havana Tonka Is a Gourmand With a Dark Side
articles.summary: Introducing Havana Tonka, the latest extrait from Byredo's Night Veils collection. A take on a grown-up gourmand, the scent mingles tonka bean, bergamot, rum, and pink peppercorn to capture the sensuality of the Cuban capital.
body: It’s been twenty years since Byredo’s founding, and in those two decades, the once-niche Swedish fragrance brand has become a household name. From Mojave Ghost to Bal D’Afrique, its scents line the fragrance walls of the industry’s most fabulous faces, practically fly off retailers’s virtual shelves, and admittedly, help set the standard of what an indie brand could be.

Formulated as an extrait, the fragrance uses high-concentration essential oils, which naturally last longer. “The idea is to create fragrances that feel rich, expressive, and full of character, with an emphasis on the depth and complexity of the ingredients,” Epinette explains. “I love the creative freedom that comes with working in this format, where you can really push certain facets of a fragrance and create something with a strong, distinctive presence.” Per Epinette, it’s less about making the fragrance shout its presence as it enters the room and more about adding depth and richness to its overall composition.

articles.title: We’ve Been Testing Great Jones Cookware for a Year — And We Totally Get Why It’s the Internet’s Favorite Brand
articles.summary: There’s something about fun, colorful cookware that makes me want to be in the kitchen more. Great Jones makes some of the most beautiful cookware I’ve ever seen — and I’ve tested more cookware than I can even count.
body: Yes. Four of our team members — myself included — have been testing Great Jones cookware over the course of the past year. We’ve loved it for its vibrant colors and fun patterns, as well as its high-quality feel. See our product recommendations at the very end.

Great Jones started in 2018, so it doesn’t have the same history as legendary brands like Le Creuset. The women-run company made a splash with its stunning cookware sold in vibrant blue, green, yellow, and pink shades. Great Jones has slowly expanded over the years and offers sleek stainless steel and ceramic nonstick pans, along with enameled cast iron, plus kitchen tools and accessories, including a cutting board, colander, whisk, baking mats, and more.

While the cookware’s colorful designs stand out, that doesn’t mean it’s all style and no substance. It’s high-quality, too. One thing all the pots and pans have in common? They’re all oven-save up to 500°F and dishwasher-safe (although hand-washing is preferred for some of the cookware). Not to mention, they all share a feature I absolutely love: no rivets! So you won’t get caught up scrubbing stuck-on food off them for what feels like forever.

articles.title: This New Garmin Feature Is Draining Battery Life, but There's a Quick Fix
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Garmin users are taking to the company's support forums with a common grievance: The newly introduced "OK Garmin" hands-free voice feature appears to be eating through battery life.
body: Last month's updates for select watches also brought all-day fall detection, a set of new Quick Workouts and Garmin Run Coach plans, as well as that "OK Garmin" hands-free voice command feature. It's exactly what it sounds like: Instead of pressing a button, users can simply say “OK Garmin” to activate voice commands. However, it looks like "OK Garmin" in particular is what causes some watch's projected runtimes to drastically drop, allegedly by roughly 35% to 50% in some cases.

Garmin does acknowledge that enabling these settings shortens battery life, though it doesn't say by how much. The tradeoff makes sense, since the watch has to listen constantly for its wake phrase. Even so, giving up several days of runtime is a steep price for a feature that many people may seldom use. Luckily, the fix is simple: Turning off "OK Garmin" should restore your battery life estimates right away.
points: Garmin users are taking to the company's support forums with a common grievance: The newly introduced "OK Garmin" hands-free voice feature appears to be eating through battery life.

articles.title: Not Cheddar, Not American — Grilled Cheese Is So Much Creamier When You Use This Cheese
articles.summary: A warm, gooey grilled cheese is my go-to dinner when I don’t have many groceries in the fridge or much energy left in my tank. I’m usually using some sort of leftover cheese, so that’s often shredded cheddar and sliced provolone. No matter what I’m using, it’s always delicious.
body: Some might argue that a side of tomato soup is the only correct answer to that question, but I would say that cheese choice is where the real answer lies. I surveyed our team for the best cheese to use in this classic sandwich and got some great responses. One person from St. Louis recommended the regional specialty cheese of Provel, a combination of cheddar, Swiss, and provolone cheeses. What I was even more interested in was the more easily accessible cheese that Food Editor Andrea Rivera Wawrzyn explained was a “sharp American cheese.” Andrea suggested Cooper Sharp White.

Our editors are big fans of using American cheese in a grilled cheese. It delivers an unreal cheese pull and melts so wonderfully so that every bite is ooey and gooey. Andrea actually wrote an explainer story about American cheese, and wrote that it was originally developed in Switzerland as a way to reduce waste. Instead of starting with milk or cream and separating the curds from the whey, American cheese is made from a blend of other cheeses and combined with emulsifiers to make it smooth.

articles.title: This Backyard Wedding in Seattle Was Inspired by Ralph Lauren and ’00s Rom-Coms
articles.summary: Stylist Sara Walker married Joe Ratliffe in her parents’ backyard, wearing vintage Vivienne Westwood, bespoke Phillipa Lepley, Emilia Wickstead, and runway Chanel over the course of the weekend.
body: Sara Walker and Joe Ratliffe’s families have known each other for over 40 years, yet the two never met until they were seniors in high school. “Our dads worked together, and we grew up just a few miles apart in Seattle—but somehow never really crossed paths until New Year’s Eve going into 2016,” Sara tells Vogue. “We shared a midnight kiss and the rest is history!”

The two dated through their senior year, then navigated long distance through college and starting jobs in different cities. “I was building my career in fashion buying, while Joe was working as a documentary filmmaker in Jackson Hole,” says Sara. “We really learned how to grow up both together and independently, even while living across different time zones.”

articles.title: Jackson, Wyoming Guide: Where to Stay, Eat, and Shop All Year Round
articles.summary: Where to stay, eat, and play in the gateway to Jackson, Wyoming, the gateway to Yellowstone National Park and home of Jackson Hole Ski resort.
body: Avid skiers champion Jackson Hole, Wyoming, for its slopeside action. Nature lovers, artists (Ansel Adams found a muse in the Snake River), and outdoor adventurers know the gateway to Yellowstone and Grand Teton National Parks is more than just a winter sports destination. It’s a four-season playground for wildlife safaris, fly fishing, foliage-filled fall hikes, and, of course, shredding fresh powder. Jackson Hole is a place where purple mountain majesties aren’t just something you sing about, and American bison (colloquially called buffalo) do, in fact, roam.

Even before touching down, visitors are welcomed in true American West style by the splendor of the Tetons, the winding river, and the verdant valley in all its glory—Jackson Hole Airport (JAC) is the only commercial airport in the United States set inside a national park. Once on the ground, the vast expanse becomes more discernible in its nuance and beauty, studded with old ranches, sagebrush-covered plains, and herds of elk.

articles.title: I Finally Decluttered My Spice Cabinet with This $18 Space-Saving Organizer
articles.summary: I moved into my first New York City apartment almost a year ago. She’s small but she’s mighty, and my roommates and I have recently decided to renew our lease. That means we’re finally dealing with all of those slight annoyances and easy fixes we’ve been putting off.
body: I had to put a lot of thought into which organizers I selected because of how narrow my cabinets are. I also wanted to get a mix of organizers to match the mix of products stored in the cabinet. Sure, there are a lot of spices, but there are also a lot of oils, vinegars, and sauces of varying sizes. After deciding on an adjustable spice shelf, clean bins, and clear stackable shelves, I took everything out of the cabinet, gave everything a good clean, and took inventory of what I actually use.

I knew I wanted an adjustable shelf for the bottom because it’s where I keep my everyday ingredients. This includes all the seasoning blends and spices I reach for practically every time I’m cooking, so I wanted to be able to see all of the bottles when I open the cabinet.

This bamboo shelf is tiered so you can see all of your bottles at first glance without picking up every individual bottle to see what the label says. It’s also adjustable, so it can match the width of your cabinet (in case you’re blessed to have more space than me).
